title: A Homecoming for the Prom
premise: Rosalind Thornbury, a trans boy starting senior year at Marrow Creek High—a school built on the flooded ruins of the town's original settlement—has one plan: stay invisible until graduation. But the college essay prompt 'What inheritance will you refuse?' cracks him open, and his answers, posted anonymously online, go viral within the school. As prom and the spring drama audition approach, Rosalind must choose between the safe girl everyone remembers and the boy he's becoming, discovering that the town itself buried its past the same way he buried his—and that belonging means claiming your name out loud. He ends the book walking into prom under his real name, having lost some friends, gained himself, and turned his essay into the audition monologue that finally lets him be seen.
about_author: Tamsin Dunmore is a former high school drama teacher from the Pacific Northwest who writes stories about kids finding their footing in towns that would rather forget. She lives in a house older than her street and collects flood maps.

chapters.title: The New Kid Who Isn't New
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. First day at Marrow Creek High, where everyone remembers 'Rose' from middle school but nobody recognizes the boy in front of them. He lets the mistake stand. Emotional beat: the exhausting relief of anonymity.

chapters.title: Built Over Something Old
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A history teacher mentions the school sits atop the drowned old town of Marrow Creek, sealed after the 1954 flood. Rosalind feels an odd kinship with something buried. Beat: eerie curiosity.

chapters.title: Rules of Invisibility
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He maps the social terrain: sit near exits, never volunteer, answer to anything. His mother, thrilled he's 'settling in,' uses the wrong name at dinner. Beat: quiet ache masked as compliance.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. English class receives the college essay prompt: 'What inheritance will you refuse?' The question lodges in him like a splinter. Beat: unease turning to obsession.

chapters.title: Draft One, Burned
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He writes three pages of truth at 2 a.m., then deletes it and submits a bland placeholder about 'resilience.' Beat: self-betrayal and the taste of ash.

chapters.title: The Understudy
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Drama teacher Ms. Okonkwo recruits him for stage crew on the spring play, sensing something. He agrees only because crew is invisible by definition. Beat: reluctant yes.

chapters.title: An Anonymous Answer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. On the school forum's anonymous essay thread, he posts one honest paragraph about refusing an inheritance of silence. By morning it has forty replies. Beat: terrified exhilaration.

chapters.title: Who Wrote That?
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The school buzzes over 'Inheritance Anon.' Popular girl Priya defends the essay in class; jock Deke calls it attention-seeking. Rosalind says nothing. Beat: vertigo of being discussed.

chapters.title: Flood Maps
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Researching the old town for set design, he finds photos of Marrow Creek before the flood—including Thornburys on the founding registry. Beat: inheritance literally surfacing.

chapters.title: Priya
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, assigned to partner with Rosalind on sets, notices he flinches at his deadname and starts quietly using 'Ros.' Beat: first crack of being known.

chapters.title: Second Post
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Emboldened, he writes about names—what we're given versus what fits. The thread explodes; someone guesses the author is a senior. Beat: momentum he can't stop.

chapters.title: Mother Knows Best
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. Rosalind's mother finds a printed draft in his room, assumes it's fiction, and praises his 'imagination.' She misses the point entirely. Beat: dramatic irony and heartbreak.

chapters.title: Auditions Announced
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ms. Okonkwo announces auditions for the lead in the spring play—a role written for any actor willing to claim it. Crew members may audition. Rosalind's stomach drops. Beat: temptation.

chapters.title: Deke's Theory
chapters.summary: Deke's POV. Deke suspects the anonymous writer is someone 'with something to hide' and starts a guessing game that feels like a hunt. Beat: menace in the hallway.

chapters.title: The Retention Pond
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He visits the retention pond behind the school—the last visible remnant of the flood—and meets groundskeeper Walt, who remembers the old town firsthand. Beat: unexpected mentorship.

chapters.title: Walt's Story
chapters.summary: Walt's POV. Walt recounts how the town chose to bury its history rather than grieve it, and how his own family name was 'corrected' at Ellis Island. Beat: parallel inheritance, gentle wisdom.

chapters.title: Third Post
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He writes about the flood, the buried town, and burying yourself to survive. It goes district-wide viral; the principal asks teachers to find the author. Beat: rising stakes.

chapters.title: Caught Between
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya figures out Rosalind is Inheritance Anon from a phrase he mutters while painting flats. She keeps his secret but urges him to sign his work. Beat: loyalty tested.

chapters.title: The Deadname Roster
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The official audition list prints his legal name. Seeing it in ink, he almost quits everything. Beat: lowest ebb so far.

chapters.title: Halfway Under
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. A panic attack in the flooded basement archives during set research; Walt finds him and sits with him in the dark. Beat: crisis and first honest conversation aloud.

chapters.title: What I Refuse
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He drafts the real college essay—about refusing the inheritance of hiding—in one unbroken sitting. He doesn't delete it this time. Beat: resolve kindling.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya risks her own social standing defending Anon publicly; Deke turns suspicion toward her. She doesn't give Rosalind up. Beat: costly friendship.

chapters.title: Mother Finds Out
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. The essay draft, left deliberately visible, confirms what Rosalind couldn't say. His mother's reaction is grief, not rage—mourning the daughter she invented. Beat: painful, human confrontation.

chapters.title: Cold House
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Days of silence at home. He sleeps at Walt's spare room once, learning Walt lost a son who never came home either. Beat: chosen family forming.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Deke's POV. Deke obtains the audition roster and outs Rosalind as both Anon and 'really Rose' in a group chat. By lunch, everyone knows. Beat: exposure, the thing he feared most.

chapters.title: Hallways After
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The school splits: some mock, some rally. Strangers Rosalind never met tell him his essays saved them. Beat: shame colliding with unexpected solidarity.

chapters.title: Ms. Okonkwo's Offer
chapters.summary: Ms. Okonkwo's POV. She reveals she knew who Anon was from post two, and offers him the audition slot officially, under whatever name he chooses to say aloud. Beat: door held open.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Terrified, he refuses the audition and asks to stay on crew forever. Priya calls him a coward with love. Beat: retreat before the final turn.

chapters.title: The Essay Submitted
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He submits his college application with the true essay, signed with his real name—an act with no audience, which makes it harder. Beat: private courage preceding public.

chapters.title: Mother, Reading
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. She reads his submitted essay (he shares the file) and, for the first time, uses his name correctly in a sentence, haltingly. Not acceptance yet—but movement. Beat: thaw.

chapters.title: Prom Politics
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Prom approaches; a petition demands Anon be banned from attending 'as himself.' Priya organizes counter-support. Beat: community taking sides.

chapters.title: Walt's Key
chapters.summary: Walt's POV. Walt gives Rosalind a key to the archives and tells him the town survived the flood not by forgetting but by rebuilding on top with open eyes. Beat: thematic key delivered.

chapters.title: Decision at the Pond
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. At the retention pond at dusk, Rosalind decides: he will audition, say his name aloud, and go to prom as himself. Beat: the turn.

chapters.title: The Audition
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. He walks onstage, states 'My name is Rosalind Thornbury—I go by Ros,' and performs a monologue built from his own essay. The room goes silent, then erupts. Beat: climax of identity.

chapters.title: Cast List
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Rosalind wins the lead; Deke, confronted by teammates who respect Ros's audition, backs down publicly if not privately. Beat: victory with residue.

chapters.title: Reckoning with Mother
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. She attends rehearsal unannounced, watches her son take the stage, and weeps—not for the daughter she lost but for the years he hid. Beat: reconciliation begun, not finished.

chapters.title: Prom Night
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Ros enters prom under the marquee reading his chosen name, flanked by Priya and Walt as invited guest chaperone. Beat: belonging achieved, joy earned.

chapters.title: The Flooded Floor
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. During prom, a pipe bursts—water seeping across the gym floor, echoing the old flood. Instead of panic, the school laughs and dances through it. Beat: symbolic release.

chapters.title: Acceptance Letter
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. An acceptance email arrives from his first-choice college, addressed to Rosalind Thornbury. He reads it aloud to Walt in the archives. Beat: future opening.

chapters.title: What I Keep
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV, epilogue. At graduation, Ros speaks briefly about inheritance: what he refused, and what he chooses to carry—Walt's stories, Priya's loyalty, his own name. Beat: resolution, wholeness, forward motion.
